dedupe_keys.name: pypsa ph high resolution open source power system model for the philippines

description: PyPSA-PH is an open-source power system model of the Philippines with high spatial and hourly temporal resolution, built on the PyPSA framework. It was released in June 2025 by Arizeo Salac of the University of Pisa with Paul Bertheau, Davide Fioriti and Jan Carsten, to support research, planning and scenario analysis for renewable integration, grid modernisation and energy policy in the Philippines. The baseline model has 192 buses, 425 generation units, 236 transmission lines and 25 storage units, with demand benchmarked to 2023 and hourly steps for a full year, using actual Philippine system data for topology, generation, storage and time series. Buses can be aggregated by trading node, administrative, provincial or district regions, and built-in functions project demand growth, CO2 reduction and hydrogen sector coupling, with plots of topology, dispatch, generation mix, levelised costs and emissions. Coverage is the Philippine grid. The notebook and data are accessible on GitHub and downloadable from Zenodo under CC BY 4.0 at no cost. Caveats: it is a single notebook, future scenarios need much memory, and the accompanying paper was still in preparation. Simulation uses are capacity expansion and dispatch studies for Philippine energy transition planning. Related records: model-pypsa is the underlying framework.
